title: Illinois 1937
bigQuestion: What does the year 1937 mark in Illinois wrestling, and what does it not mark?

story.title: Names Under a State Seal
story.kicker: An old program shows the first year Illinois named high school wrestling champions.
paragraphs: Picture a student in an Illinois library. She opens a folder of old papers. Inside is a thin program from 1937. At the top are a state seal and the name of the state's high school association.
Below the seal are lists. Each list has a weight at the top. Under each weight are names of boys and the high schools they came from. The paper is yellow and soft at the edges.
In 1937, the association named its first state champions in wrestling. One boy won in each weight class. His name went into the state record. That record has grown every winter since.

The student looks at the date again. Wrestling in Illinois did not begin that year. Abraham Lincoln wrestled at New Salem more than a hundred years earlier. Paid wrestlers filled Chicago arenas before 1937 too.
So what began in 1937? A school contest began, with a state seal, a scale and a written list. The program marks the start of a record, not the start of a sport.
story.think: Why might the first year of a state title be a different date from the first year of a sport?

sections.title: The Body That Runs School Sports

lessons.title: An Association Since 1900
lessons.mainIdea: The Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, is the group of member schools that runs state contests in Illinois.
reading: In the late 1800s, students often ran their own school teams. They set their own schedules. Some players were not even students. School leaders wanted fair, shared rules for every team.

In 1900, Illinois schools formed a state *association*. An association is a group that joins together under one set of rules. Today it is called the *IHSA*, the Illinois High School Association. Its main office is in Bloomington, Illinois.

High schools choose to become *member schools* of the IHSA. They agree to follow its rules. The IHSA decides who may play, and it runs the state series. A state series is the set of contests that ends with state champions.

words.d: a group that joins together under one set of rules
the Illinois High School Association, founded in 1900, which runs high school state contests
schools that join an association and agree to follow its rules

look.title: Before and After an Association
look.text: Before: each school team makes its own rules. One team lets older men play. Another does not. After: every member school signs on to one rule book. Every team knows who may play and how the champion is chosen.
look.prompt: Why would schools want one shared rule book?

check.q: When was the IHSA founded?
check.why: The IHSA was founded in 1900. 1937 was its first wrestling championship.

check.q: What is an association?
choices: a group that joins together under one set of rules
check.why: An association joins members under one set of rules.

check.q: Where is the IHSA's main office?
check.why: The IHSA's main office is in Bloomington, Illinois.

lessons.title: The Rule Book and the Scale
lessons.mainIdea: Illinois high school wrestling follows the NFHS rule book, which sets weight classes and a weigh-in before each meet.
reading: State associations share one national rule book for each high school sport. The *NFHS* writes these books. It first met in Chicago in 1920. Illinois high schools follow its wrestling rules.
The rule book sets the *weight classes*. For boys, it lists 14 classes. They run from 106 pounds up to 285 pounds. Each wrestler meets only people in the same class.
Before each meet, wrestlers step on a scale. This is called the *weigh-in*. It shows which class each wrestler may enter. The rule book is updated often, so rules can change from year to year.

words.d: National Federation of State High School Associations, which writes high school rule books
groups that match wrestlers who are close in body weight
the time before a meet when each wrestler is weighed on a scale

check.why: The NFHS lists 14 boys' classes. The NCAA has 10.

check.q: Who writes the rule book Illinois high schools use for wrestling?
check.why: Illinois high schools follow the NFHS wrestling rules.

lessons.title: Champions by Weight, 1937
lessons.mainIdea: In 1937, the IHSA named its first boys' state wrestling champions, one in each weight class.
reading: The IHSA crowned its first state champions in boys' wrestling in 1937. That was 37 years after the association began. By then, the IHSA already ran state contests in other sports, such as basketball and track.

A wrestling state final is a *tournament*. A tournament is a contest with many matches that ends with one winner. Wrestlers are placed in a *bracket*. A bracket is a chart that shows who meets whom in each round.
Each weight class has its own bracket. So a state final names many champions, not just one. Teams earn points from their wrestlers' wins. Each champion's name joins the IHSA's written record.

words.d: a contest with many matches that ends with one winner
a chart that shows who meets whom in each round of a tournament
the winner of a state final in one class or division

look.title: One Final, Many Champions
look.text: At a basketball state final, one team wins the title. At a wrestling state final, the room holds many brackets at once. When the day ends, there is one champion in every weight class. There can also be a team title.
look.prompt: Why does a wrestling final name so many champions?

check.q: When did the IHSA name its first boys' wrestling state champions?
check.why: The first IHSA boys' wrestling state champions were crowned in 1937.

check.q: What is a bracket?
choices: a chart of who meets whom in each round
check.why: A bracket shows who meets whom in each round of a tournament.

check.q: Why does a wrestling state final name many champions?
choices: Each weight class has its own bracket.
check.why: Each weight class has its own bracket and its own champion.

lessons.title: Reading an Old Program
lessons.mainIdea: An old meet program is a primary source that can show names, schools and weights, but not everything that happened.
reading: A *program* is a printed paper handed out at an event. A wrestling program lists the weight classes. It lists the wrestlers and their schools. It may show the date, the place and the seal of the association.
A program from 1937 is a *primary source*. It was made at the time being studied. Historians use programs, newspapers and school yearbooks together. Each one can check the others.
A program also has limits. It is printed before the matches, so it cannot tell who won. It may leave out people who were not allowed to enter. Historians ask who is missing, as well as who is listed.

words.d: a printed paper handed out at an event, listing who takes part
something made at the time being studied

look.title: Questions for a Program
look.text: You hold a printed program from a state wrestling meet in the 1930s. It lists weight classes. Under each class are names and high schools. Every name is a boy's name. There are no scores on the page.
look.prompt: Name one thing this program tells you and one thing you would need another source to learn.

check.q: Why is a 1937 program a primary source?
choices: It was made at the time being studied.
It was written by a historian today.
It is the first page of a book.
It is about the first Olympics.
check.why: A primary source is made at the time being studied.

check.q: Why can a program printed before a meet not tell who won?
choices: It was printed before the matches.
check.why: A program is printed ahead of time, so the results come from other sources.

check.q: What else do historians use to check a program?
check.why: Historians compare programs, newspapers and yearbooks to check each other.

lessons.title: A Start Line, Not a Birthday
lessons.mainIdea: The year 1937 marks the start of a school record in Illinois, not the invention of wrestling.
reading: People sometimes treat a first championship as the birthday of a sport. For wrestling, that would be a big mistake. Egyptian tomb paintings of wrestlers are about 4,000 years old. Greek wrestling joined the Olympic Games in 708 BCE.
What 1937 marks is a *record*. A record is a written list kept over time. The IHSA has kept its wrestling champions list every year since. The list lets people compare schools and years.
Many dates in school sports work this way. They mark when a body began counting. The NCAA held its first wrestling championship in 1928. The IHSA held its first girls' wrestling state finals in 2022.

words.d: a written list of results kept over time
the first making of something new

choices: the start of the IHSA's wrestling champions record
check.why: 1937 marks the first IHSA boys' state champions, the start of a record.

check.q: Which is the oldest?
check.why: The Egyptian paintings are about 4,000 years old. The others are from the 1900s.

choices: a written list of results kept over time
check.why: A record is a written list kept over time, like the IHSA champions list.

lessons.title: Lincoln at New Salem
lessons.mainIdea: In 1831, young Abraham Lincoln wrestled Jack Armstrong at New Salem, Illinois, long before any school title.
reading: In 1831, Abraham Lincoln moved to *New Salem*, a small village on the Sangamon River in Illinois. He was about 22 years old. He worked as a clerk in a store owned by Denton Offutt.

Offutt bragged that Lincoln could beat any man around. A group of young men from nearby Clary's Grove took up the challenge. Their leader, Jack Armstrong, wrestled Lincoln. Old accounts disagree about who won, but they agree the two became friends.

William Herndon, Lincoln's law partner, told the story in his book, *Herndon's Lincoln*, in 1889. The match had no weight classes and no clock. Much later, the National Wrestling Hall of Fame honored Lincoln as an Outstanding American.

words.d: a village on the Sangamon River in Illinois where Lincoln lived in the 1830s
a story or report of what happened, told by a person
an 1889 book about Lincoln by his law partner William Herndon

look.title: A Match at New Salem
look.text: Offutt boasted that his clerk could outrun, outlift and outwrestle any man around. The Clary's Grove boys chose Jack Armstrong to test him. The match drew a crowd. Afterward Armstrong and Lincoln were friends.
look.cite: William H. Herndon and Jesse W. Weik, Herndon's Lincoln (1889)
look.prompt: Herndon wrote this almost 60 years after the match. What might that mean for the details?

check.q: Where did Lincoln wrestle Jack Armstrong?
check.why: The match was at New Salem, a village on the Sangamon River.

check.q: Who told the story in an 1889 book?
check.why: William Herndon, Lincoln's law partner, told it in Herndon's Lincoln.

check.q: What do old accounts agree on about the match?
choices: that Lincoln and Armstrong became friends
check.why: Accounts disagree about who won but agree the two became friends.

lessons.title: Frank Gotch in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: In 1908 and 1911, Frank Gotch beat George Hackenschmidt in Chicago in famous professional matches.
reading: Frank Gotch was a farm boy from Humboldt, Iowa. He became a *professional* wrestler. A professional is paid to take part in a sport. In the early 1900s, pro wrestling matches drew big crowds and filled newspapers.

On April 3, 1908, Gotch met George Hackenschmidt in Chicago. Hackenschmidt was born in Estonia, then part of the Russian Empire. People called him the Russian Lion. Gotch won and became world heavyweight champion.

In 1911, they met again at Comiskey Park, the new home of the Chicago White Sox. A huge crowd came. Gotch won again. Later in the 1900s, pro wrestling turned into a planned show. School wrestlers stayed *amateurs*, who are not paid.

words.d: a person paid to take part in a sport
people who take part in a sport without being paid

look.title: A Ballpark Becomes a Wrestling Room
look.text: It is 1911 on the South Side of Chicago. A baseball park built the year before is full of people. A raised ring stands where the ball game usually is. Two paid wrestlers climb in. Newspapers across the country will print the result.
look.prompt: How is this room different from a high school gym at a state final?

check.q: Where was Frank Gotch from?
check.why: Gotch was a farm boy from Humboldt, Iowa.

check.q: What is a professional?
choices: a student on a school team
a person paid to take part in a sport
a person who writes rule books
check.why: A professional is paid. School wrestlers are amateurs.

check.q: Where did Gotch and Hackenschmidt meet in 1911?
check.why: Their 1911 rematch was at Comiskey Park, home of the White Sox.

lessons.title: Title IX, 1972
lessons.mainIdea: Title IX, a 1972 law, says schools that get federal money cannot shut people out because of their sex.
reading: For most of the 1900s, school wrestling in Illinois was for boys. The 1937 program had only boys' names. Many schools had few sports of any kind for girls.

In 1972, Congress passed the Education Amendments. One part is called *Title IX*. President Richard Nixon signed it on June 23, 1972. It covers schools and colleges that get money from the *federal* government.

Title IX says those schools cannot leave people out because of their sex. Over time, schools added many girls' teams. For years, girls who wanted to wrestle joined the boys' team. Some of them were the only girl in the room.

words.d: a 1972 U.S. law that bans shutting people out of school programs because of sex
belonging to the national government of the United States

look.title: The Words of Title IX
look.text: No person in the United States shall, on the basis of sex, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any education program or activity receiving Federal financial assistance.
look.cite: Title IX, Education Amendments of 1972, section 901(a)
look.prompt: Put this sentence in your own words. Which schools does it cover?

check.q: When was Title IX signed?
check.why: President Nixon signed Title IX on June 23, 1972.

check.q: Which schools does Title IX cover?
check.why: Title IX covers education programs that receive federal financial help.

check.q: Before girls' teams, how did many girls wrestle in school?
check.why: For years, girls who wanted to wrestle joined the boys' team.

lessons.title: Girls' State Finals, 2022
lessons.mainIdea: The IHSA held its first girls' wrestling state finals in the 2021–22 season, 85 years after the first boys' champions.
reading: As more girls joined wrestling, states began to hold separate girls' contests. Women's wrestling had joined the Olympics in Athens in 2004. That gave girls famous wrestlers to look up to.
In Illinois, the IHSA held its first *girls' state finals* in wrestling in 2022. That was during the 2021–22 school year. It came 85 years after the first boys' champions in 1937.

The first girls' champions started a new line in the IHSA record. Their weight classes are set for girls. From 2022 on, each year adds new names to both lists. Historians can now compare how the two lists grow.

words.d: the state championship for girls' wrestling; the IHSA held its first in 2022
set apart as its own group

look.title: Two Lists in One Record
look.text: Picture two lists of champions on the same wall. The boys' list starts in 1937. It is long, with names from every year. The girls' list starts in 2022. It is short, but a new row is added each winter.
look.prompt: What does the difference in length tell you about when doors opened?

check.q: When were the first IHSA girls' wrestling state finals?
check.why: The first IHSA girls' state finals were in 2022, during the 2021–22 season.

check.q: How many years after the first boys' champions did the girls' finals come?
check.why: From 1937 to 2022 is 85 years.

check.q: When did women's wrestling join the Olympics?
check.why: Women's wrestling joined the Olympics in Athens in 2004.

lessons.title: A Champion Born With One Leg
lessons.mainIdea: Anthony Robles, born with one leg, won the NCAA wrestling title at 125 pounds in 2011.
reading: Anthony Robles was born in 1988 with only one leg. He grew up in Mesa, Arizona. He began wrestling as a young teenager. He used crutches to get around, not a prosthetic leg.

Robles wrestled in college for Arizona State University. In 2011, he won the *NCAA* championship at 125 pounds. He did not lose a match that whole season. The NCAA is the body that runs most college sports.

Robles showed that wrestling rooms can include many kinds of bodies. The weight class rule mattered here too. It matched him with people of the same weight. His story is told in his book, Unstoppable, published in 2012.

words.d: the National Collegiate Athletic Association, which runs most college sports
made to take the place of a missing body part

look.text: In 1831, the New Salem match had no written rules at all. In 1937, the Illinois program had only boys' names. In 2011, a college wrestler born with one leg won a national title. In 2022, Illinois girls wrestled for their own state crown.
